summary: Valise stolen from a train at the Gare de Lyon
story: On July 2 I took the train from Paris to Lausanne to join my husband, who was working there. At the Gare de Lyon I put my valise on the luggage rack in our carriage and stepped off the train to buy a bottle of water for the journey. I was gone for perhaps ten minutes. When I came back the valise was gone. It held my clothes and, far worse, all of my husband's writing: the printed manuscript of his novel, his notebooks and the backup drive, which I had packed so that he could work on everything in Switzerland. There are no other copies. I reported it to the police at the station that afternoon. I have valued the manuscript and notebooks at $1,900, though my husband would call that figure an insult.

documents.name: Police report
documents.content: Police Nationale, Gare de Lyon, Paris. Report 2026/071845, filed July 2, 2026 at 14:20 by Hadley Richards, US citizen. The complainant states that she placed a brown leather valise on the luggage rack of carriage 12 of the 12:57 service to Lausanne, left the train to make a purchase on the platform and returned about ten minutes later to find the valise missing. No witnesses. No suspect identified.

documents.name: List of contents
documents.content: Leather valise: $320. Clothing and shoes for two weeks: $610. Printed manuscript, about 400 pages, and six notebooks: $1,900. Backup drive, 1 TB: $70.
